Keywords: Cargo disputes at the Daugava mouth
RagShortTexts: Riga links inland Daugava routes and the sea under differing church, Order and civic rights.
Unloading, charges and cargo disputes need recognized authorities; delays add merchants' costs.

Variants.Content: Riga connects seagoing ships and inland carriage through the Daugava mouth, while archbishop, Order and townsmen pursue distinct interests. Cargo needs unloading, storage and inspection under a recognizable jurisdiction. Shipping and safe routes bring revenue; excessive demands or disputed rights can delay or divert merchants and weaken town trade.

Riga's porters, boatmen and small sellers depend on moving cargo. Waiting consumes lodging and food; hurried unloading damages goods. Familiar witnesses help when charges are questioned. Residents want a safe harbor whose guards and collectors leave enough movement for them to earn their daily food.
